messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — streaming endpoints (SSE/WebSocket) in prod showing increased tail latency and stall reports. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~950ms, p99 ~2.6s -> ~6.8s in us-east-1. Rolling error budget burn. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/streams?range=15m :rotating_light:

alice: i'm on pager, looking now. which service is the hotspot? any customer impact flags?

bob: I see the same in infra metrics — streaming-proxy p99 write latency spiking, a handful of 502/504s from the proxy to runtime. No bulk model OOMs.

carla: runtime-side looks healthy, KV cache hitrates normal. connections to model backend stable. suspecting buffering/backpressure at the proxy layer or slow consumers.

dave: support reported 3 customers with interrupted streams in the last 10m (ticket ids: #3482 #3487 #3490). one reported repeated reconnects after ~30s.

erin: Observability: socket_write_time_ms and tcp_send_queue are both high on streaming-proxy pods. Here's a quick log tail showing the pattern:

```
2026-03-15T02:10:12Z streaming-proxy-3 app INFO chunk flush delayed (socket_write=420ms, backlog=128)
2026-03-15T02:10:14Z streaming-proxy-1 app WARN upstream write timeout 1.5s -> 504
2026-03-15T02:10:18Z streaming-proxy-2 kernel WARN tcp_send_queue full for socket id 0x7f3b
```

alice: thanks erin. can we confirm whether this is client-side slow consumers (mobile NAT connections) or server-side throttle? any correlation with a specific client user-agent?

erin: sampling shows a mix, but a noticeable cluster of user-agent "Redwood-Client/1.8" coming from same ASNs. also an increase in concurrent connections per socket from some IPs. suggests slow consumers + head-of-line blocking in the proxy.

bob: immediate mitigation options: 1) scale streaming-proxy replicas, 2) reduce proxy buffer sizes and flush intervals, 3) enable per-connection backpressure timeouts to drop very slow consumers early, 4) route high-concurrency clients to dedicated path. propose scaling + config change as hotfix.

carla: agree. runtime can handle more upstream qps. if we scale proxies quickly we should relieve socket pressure. also suggest temporarily lowering per-connection max duration for SSE in the proxy (e.g., max_time 120s) so slow clients don't hog fds.

alice: do it. bob, can you run scale and config patch? i'll coordinate customer comms.

bob: executing now — patching deployment and increasing replicas from 3->8 in us-east-1:

```bash
kubectl scale deployment streaming-proxy -n prod --replicas=8
kubectl patch configmap streaming-proxy-conf -n prod --patch '{"data":{"proxy_buffering":"off","flush_interval_ms":"50","max_idle_timeout_s":"120"}}'
```

pager-bot: PagerDuty: alice acknowledged the incident. escalation to eng-sre if not resolved in 15 minutes.

~2m later~

bob: replicas are up, new pods passing readiness. traffic rebalanced. initial metrics show p95 decreased to ~220ms but p99 still elevated (~1.3s).

carla: rolled the proxy config (flush_interval_ms=50, proxy_buffering=off). also set keepalive_timeout lower. early signs look positive: socket_write_ms median dropped, retransmits down.

dave: support update — customers #3482 and #3490 reporting streams now stable, #3487 still saw one drop then recovered. sending holding message to affected customers.

erin: telemetry shows backlog depth decreasing but periodic spikes remain at ~2% of connections. digging into those flows now — they look like long-poll clients on flaky mobile networks.

alice: good. containment seems effective. decision: keep scaled replicas and config for 2 hours, watch for recurrence. start RCA and assign follow-ups.

bob: creating temporary alert to flag socket_write_time_ms > 200ms and connection_queue > 100 for any single pod. patching alert now.

carla: follow-ups: (1) improve proxy eviction for stuck slow consumers (per-connection rate limit + graceful drop), (2) add streaming probe that simulates slow consumer to reproduce locally, (3) evaluate TCP tuning (sndbuf/txqueuelen) on host, (4) quick docs for customers about recommended client keepalive. I'll own 1+2.

alice: assign tasks and handoff: carla -> lead on engineering fix, bob -> revert scale/config to safer defaults after monitoring window, erin -> post-incident dashboard and fine-grained metrics, dave -> finalize customer comms, alice -> postmortem owner.

dave: sending follow-up email to affected customers with mitigation summary + contact.

alice: marking incident as 'mitigated' in the channel. setting follow-up meeting at 2026-03-15T10:00Z for RCA and action items. thanks all. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated: p95 ~140ms, p99 ~720ms. total impacted requests estimated 0.8% of streaming traffic over last 30m. incident severity: SEV2 -> tracking RCA.
